DuckDB Version Compatibility

Source: vignettes/duckdb-version-compatibility.Rmd
duckdb-version-compatibility.Rmd

Two versions

Rducks needs duckdb 2.0.0 or later. Two versions apply:

  • C API version, v1.5.6. Rducks builds its extension against DuckDB’s stable C extension API, with C_STRUCT metadata. DuckDB loads such an extension on every engine release that supports that API version, so each platform needs only one build.
  • Minimum engine version, v2.0.0. rducks_enable() loads the extension from a signed local extension repository. Extension repositories need DuckDB v2.0.0.

The installed package contains one extension and its public key:

rducks_extension/build/rducks.duckdb_extension
rducks_extension/build/rducks.pub
basename(rducks_extension_path())
#> [1] "rducks.duckdb_extension"
rducks_extension_capi_version()
#> [1] "v1.5.6"

Signed local repository

Installation signs the extension with a key generated for that installation and keeps only the public key. Nothing else can be signed with that key after installation.

rducks_enable(con) then:

  1. checks that con runs DuckDB v2.0.0 or later and that the engine supports the C API version of the extension;
  2. copies the extension below tempdir() in the repository layout <version>/<platform>/rducks.duckdb_extension, where <version> is the release tag of the engine, or its source id for a development build;
  3. sets allow_extension_repositories to 'allowed' if it has DuckDB’s default ('undecided' in 2.0.0, 'hosts' from 2.0.1), and registers the repository with the public key;
  4. runs INSTALL and LOAD from the repository, with extension_directory pointed below tempdir() during INSTALL;
  5. restores extension_directory and removes the repository record.

DuckDB’s signature checks stay enabled: allow_unsigned_extensions is not needed, and a modified file fails to load.

DuckDB writes the repository record to extension_repository_directory, which it accepts only at startup. Open connections with rducks_duckdb_config() to keep the record below tempdir():

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(config = rducks_duckdb_config(list(threads = "2"))))
rducks_enable(con)

On a connection opened without it, such as the default connection of duckplyr, the record goes to ~/.duckdb/extension_repositories until LOAD finishes. rducks_enable() does this only with home_registry = TRUE. A connection with allow_extension_repositories set to 'forbidden' or 'hosts_only' cannot load Rducks: DuckDB only tightens that setting while the database runs.

Diagnostics 

DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT library_version, source_id FROM pragma_version()")
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT current_setting('allow_extension_repositories')")
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT current_setting('extension_repository_directory')")
rducks_extension_capi_version()

An explicit extension_path skips the repository and runs a plain LOAD, so DuckDB must accept the signature of that file or the connection must allow unsigned extensions.

DuckDB 1.5.6

The backport/duckdb-1.5 branch keeps a release line for duckdb 1.5.6. It builds the same stable C API extension, does not sign it, and loads it with a plain LOAD, so connections need allow_unsigned_extensions.

Maintainer workflow

The DuckDB C API headers are vendored in tools/ext/duckdb_capi/. The duckdb_ref release recorded in duckdb_headers.json is the C API version that configure and configure.win target. To change it, vendor the headers of another release:

Rscript tools/fetch_duckdb_headers.R --ref v1.5.6

The C API version must not be newer than the minimum engine version. The minimum engine version is rducks_min_duckdb_version in R/extension_repository.R and the duckdb requirement in DESCRIPTION; a test checks that they agree. The build fails if DUCKDB_EXTENSION_API_VERSION_UNSTABLE is defined, because an unstable build would tie the artifact to one exact engine release. See docs/BUILD.md in the source repository for the native build details.
